# Output Spec — contract for every generated file

The generated artifact is a PROJECT SKILL at `.claude/skills/repo-guide/`
in the target repo. No CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or GEMINI.md files are created
or modified by the map/refresh pipeline. (The separate, explicitly invoked
init mode — see init-mode.md — writes a thin CLAUDE.md of always-loaded
rules, behind its own approval gate; it is the only mode that touches
CLAUDE.md.) Claude Code auto-discovers the skill; other tools supporting the
Agent Skills standard can consume the same folder; its content is plain
markdown any agent can be pointed at.

```
.claude/skills/repo-guide/
├── SKILL.md          # THE index — small, always-discoverable, loads on demand
└── references/
    ├── architecture.md
    ├── modules.md
    ├── symbols.md
    ├── conventions.md
    └── commands.md
```

No other files. Principle: information retrievable from git (generation
commit, staleness, edit history) is NEVER stored — it is derived (see
freshness.md). The only stored provenance is a generated-on date comment,
which carries the no-git degraded case.

Every generated markdown file starts (after frontmatter, where present) with:
`<!-- generated by repo-mapper on <YYYY-MM-DD> -->`

## SKILL.md — hard cap 100 lines including frontmatter

Frontmatter (YAML, required):
```yaml
---
name: repo-guide
description: Use when starting any task in this repository (<repo/product name>) — read before exploring or editing the codebase; routes to indexed references for architecture, module layout, symbols, conventions, and build/test commands.
---
```

Body, in order:
1. Generated-on comment + one freshness line:
   `This index is as old as the last commit touching .claude/skills/repo-guide (check: \`git log -1 -- .claude/skills/repo-guide\`). If the repo has moved much since, verify details against code before relying on them; regenerate with /repo-map refresh.`
2. **Purpose** — max 3 sentences: what this codebase is and does.
3. **Stack** — one line: languages, frameworks, package manager, runtime.
4. **Navigation table** — the routing core. `| Question | Read |` rows pointing
   into `references/`, e.g. "How is the code organized?" → `references/modules.md`;
   "Where is symbol/feature X?" → `references/symbols.md`; "How do I
   build/test/run?" → `references/commands.md`; "What patterns must new code
   follow?" → `references/conventions.md`; "How do subsystems interact?" →
   `references/architecture.md`. Plus explicit instruction: load these only
   when the task needs them.
5. **Entry points** — up to 5: main/server/CLI entry files (repo-root-relative
   paths).
6. **Gotchas** — 3-5 bullets: the non-obvious things that burn agents (weird
   build step, generated dirs, deprecated area, naming trap).

If a skill already exists at this path, regeneration replaces it — but first
check `git status --porcelain -- .claude/skills/repo-guide`: uncommitted
changes are user edits in flight; show them and ASK before overwriting
(see freshness.md). Recommend committing the regenerated index as its own
commit so history stays diffable.

## references/ files

Each self-contained and task-scoped; a typical task needs SKILL.md + 1-2 of
these. All code paths are repo-root-relative. No line numbers anywhere — file
paths only (line numbers rot too fast).

- **architecture.md** — subsystems, their responsibilities and boundaries, how
  data/requests flow between them, external services. Diagrams as ASCII/mermaid
  if they clarify.
- **modules.md** — per-directory map: `path — purpose — key files`. Covers
  every non-excluded top-level dir; depth where it earns it.
- **symbols.md** — one table: `| Symbol | Kind | File | Role |`. Key exports,
  routes, models, commands, config objects — the things an agent hunts for.
  FILE granularity only. Default cap ~150 rows — a default validated only on
  small/medium repos; on large repos prefer coverage of the public surface
  over exhaustiveness rather than raising the cap.
- **conventions.md** — naming, error handling, test style, state patterns,
  import rules — each claim tagged with an example file that exhibits it.
  Conflicts between areas are stated explicitly ("api uses X; legacy/ uses Y").
- **commands.md** — build/test/run/lint. Each entry marked `verified` (was
  actually executed this run, with exit status) or `unverified` (read from
  package scripts/docs). Only mark verified if the user consented to execution.

## Monorepo mode

One skill: SKILL.md routes to packages (table: package → path → one-liner) and
holds only repo-wide content; per-package depth goes into
`references/pkg-<name>.md` files instead of the five standard references when
packages are truly independent. Scale warning: caps and budgets in this spec
are defaults tuned on small repos — on a large monorepo, the scout's cost
estimate and the user's confirmation are the real guardrails, and the 100-line
SKILL.md must route to packages rather than trying to cover them.

## Existing fat CLAUDE.md (migration offer)

repo-mapper never writes CLAUDE.md, but if the repo has a large one, OFFER
(current → proposed table, user approval required) to migrate its
repo-knowledge content into references/ and shrink CLAUDE.md to the user's
genuinely-global rules. Never do this silently.
